newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian rates stable as liquidity improves.
newsitem.headline: Croatian rates stable as liquidity improves.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were unchanged in slow trade on Wednesday, although increased offer of term funds pointed to improved bank liquidity, dealers said.
Early trade totalled 20 million kuna, most of which, some nine million, was call money granted at an unchanged 10.5 percent rate.
The rest were 30- and 12-day loans, granted at the usual 15-16 and 11-12 percent rates, respectively.
There was 25 million left on the supply side, which indicated improved liquidity in the banking sector, one dealer said.
Only one case of demand, from a bank looking to borrow five million for 60 days, could not be matched.
The total amount of kuna funds on banks' accounts rose further to 463 million. Overnight trade totalled 55 million, as two banks borrowed to maintain mandatory reserves.
